title: DSA: Efficient Inference For Video Generation Models via Distributed Sparse Attention
claim: Dense attention dominates execution time across models, making it the main bottleneck worth targeting for acceleration.
layout: single stacked bar chart, three bars, legend at right, numbers inside segments
description: A single stacked bar chart showing execution time percentage (y-axis, 0 to 100) for three video generation models on the x-axis: wan-1.3B, wan-14B and hunyuan-13B. Each bar is split into three segments. A large orange Attention segment at the bottom takes 79, 88 and 86 percent. A blue FFN segment sits above it (13, 8, 9). A small tan Others segment is on top (8, 4, 5). Numbers are printed inside each segment. The legend is in the upper right. The tall orange blocks draw the eye first, so the reader sees at once that attention dominates runtime. The style is clean matplotlib with bold labels and thin gridlines.
caption: Execution time breakdown of 720p 5-second video generation of different models on H100 GPUs
abstract: Diffusion Transformer models have driven the rapid advances in video generation, achieving state-of-the-art quality and flexibility. However, their attention mechanism remains a major performance bottleneck, as its dense computation scales quadratically with the sequence length. To overcome this limitation and reduce the generation latency, we propose DSA, a novel attention mechanism that integrates sparse attention with distributed inference for diffusion-based video generation. By leveraging carefully-designed parallelism strategies and scheduling, DSA significantly reduces redundant computation while preserving global context. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that, when deployed on 8 GPUs, DSA achieves up to 1.43× inference speedup than the existing distributed method and 10.79× faster than single-GPU inference.
